newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan jobless rate sticks near record levels.
newsitem.headline: Japan jobless rate sticks near record levels.

text.p: Japan's jobless rate clung close to record levels last month but the government said on Tuesday that the ranks of the unemployed had been swelled by people seeking to change jobs as the economy brightens.

The nation's unemployment rate was steady at 3.3 percent in September, unchanged from August and a shade below the record 3.5 percent seen in the summer, according to official figures released on Tuesday.

Although Japan does not have the double-digit jobless rates of some Western countries, the climb in the rate seen over the past year has caused concern in a nation which has had minimal unemployment for most of the postwar era.
The government said that although the rate stayed stubbornly high, there was a silver lining in the statistics that suggested growing economic confidence and job mobility.
The figures showed that a record number of workers had voluntarily quit their jobs in September -- a total of 930,000 people, up 30,000 from a year earlier.

"Overall, we see an improving economy as a possible cause of the rise in people leaving their jobs voluntarily," a government official said. He cautioned it was too early to tell if unemployment did actually peak in May and June, when it was at 3.5 percent.

But analysts were cautious, as there have been signs recently of lingering sluggishness in the economy, whose recovery remains weak. Although the overall rate was steady, the unemployment rate among older workers edged up in September.
The total of people voluntarily leaving their jobs in September was the highest since January 1983, when the agency started collecting the jobless data.

Despite government stimulus steps, the economy has been struggling to recover from a slump which set in after the collapse of the 1980s economic "bubble", forcing companies to cut costs and restructure their operations to maintain profits.
Many economists predict that the economic recovery will slow in early 1997, especially after a planned rise in the sales tax next April to five percent from three percent.

"We cannot predict any strong and bright employment figures in the near future. My prediction is that the unemployment rate will not be below three percent for the next year or so," said Masaru Takagi, chief economist at Fuji Research Institute.
Economists say there should be drastic changes in Japan's economic structures and regulations, which have long restrained activities that could create new jobs.

Satoshi Shimamoto, a senior economist at MMS International, said Japanese companies are still using capital spending to streamline business, rather than to increase production facilities. "That's why an increase in labour force or human capital is limited," he said.

Unemployment among middle-aged or older workers is on a rising trend as companies continue to streamline operations and cut wage costs. In September, the jobless rate among workers aged over 55 rose by 0.2 percentage point from August to 5.1 percent.
The total number of employed people was 65.69 million in September, a rise of 400,000 over a year ago.
